simple.meaning: אַרְמוֹן (ʼarmôwn) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a citadel (from its height ).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 32 times across 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, Proverbs, and 6 more, beginning at 1 Kings 16:18. Its contexts include family line, death, kingship, city.

definitions.full: H759. armon אַרְמוֺן noun masculine Isa 32:14 citadel — ׳א absolute Jer 30:18 +; construct Isa 25:2 ; plural אַרְמְנוֺת absolute Amos 3:9 (twice in verse); construct 1:4 +; אַרְמְנוֺתֵינוּ Micah 5:4 +, etc. — citadel, castle, palace , not used before royal period, mostly in prophets, especially common in Amos & Jeremiah; citadel as securely barred (in simile) Prov 18:19 ; ׳א הַמֶּלֶךְ בֵּית i.e. the citadel, stronghold 1Kin 16:18 , compare 2Kin 15:25 ; usually more General, of castle, palaces , prominent buildings; especially used in speaking of conquest, because the fine buildings would be especially object of attack & plunder; palaces of Israel Amos 6:8 ; of Jerusalem Isa 32:14 (singular collective) Lam 2:5 , 7 ; 2Chr 36:19 ; Psa 48:4 ; 48:14 ; 122:7 compare Hosea 8:14 ; Micah 5:4 ; Amos 2:5 ; Jer 17:27 ; of Samaria Amos 3:10-11 , also Jer 6:5 ; 9:20 belonging to Benhadad (i.e. Aram) Amos 1:4 ; Jer 49:27 ; of Tyre Isa 23:13 ; Amos 1:10 ; of Babylon Isa 25:2 (singular collective), compare 13:22 where read אַרְמְנוֺתָיו for אלמנותיו so ᵑ9 ᵑ7 ᵑ6 Che Di (|| היכלים ; compare Ezek 19:7 according to ᵑ7 and others, but see rather מעון ; Dl BD xi defends ᵑ0 in 19:7 & compare Assyrian almattu , fortress ); of Edom Isa 34:13 , of Gaza Amos 1:7 , of Rabbah 1:14 , of Bozrah 1:12 , of Kerioth 2:2 , of Ashdod 3:9 , of Egypt 3:9 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root (meaning to be elevated );

occurrences.englishText: When Zimri saw that the city was taken, he went into the fortified part of the king’s house, and burned the king’s house over him with fire, and died,

Pekah the son of Remaliah, his captain, conspired against him and attacked him in Samaria, in the fortress of the king’s house, with Argob and Arieh; and with him were fifty men of the Gileadites. He killed him, and reigned in his place.
They burned God’s house, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem, and burned all its palaces with fire, and destroyed all of its valuable vessels.
For, behold, the kings assembled themselves,
For this God is our God forever and ever.
Peace be within your walls,
A brother offended is more difficult than a fortified city.
Behold, the land of the Chaldeans. This people didn’t exist. The Assyrians founded it for those who dwell in the wilderness. They set up their towers. They overthrew its palaces. They made it a ruin.
For you have made a city into a heap, a fortified city into a ruin, a palace of strangers to be no city. It will never be built.
For the palace will be forsaken.
Thorns will come up in its palaces,
Arise! Let’s go up by night, and let’s destroy her palaces.”
Yet hear Yahweh’s word, you women.

But if you will not listen to me to make the Sabbath day holy, and not to bear a burden and enter in at the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it will devour the palaces of Jerusalem. It will not be quenched.” ’ ”
Yahweh says:
“I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus,
The Lord has become as an enemy.
The Lord has cast off his altar.
For Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces;
but I will send a fire into the house of Hazael,
but I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza,
but I will send a fire on the wall of Tyre,
but I will send a fire on Teman,
But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah,
but I will send a fire on Moab,
but I will send a fire on Judah,
Proclaim in the palaces at Ashdod,
Proclaim in the palaces at Ashdod,
“Indeed they don’t know to do right,” says Yahweh,
Therefore the Lord Yahweh says:
“The Lord Yahweh has sworn by himself,” says Yahweh, the God of Armies:
He shall stand, and shall shepherd in the strength of Yahweh,
